Explanation:

We have a square matrix of dimension $n=2.$ Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{At} & ={\alpha }_{1}At+{\alpha }_{0}I \\  & ={\alpha }_{1}[\begin{aligned}-5 & -6 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]t+{\alpha }_{0}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & -6{\alpha }_{1}t \\ 3{\alpha }_{1}t & 4{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

where ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ are functions to be determined.

Consider the polynomial $r(\lambda )={\alpha }_{1}\lambda +{\alpha }_{0}.$ The eigenvalues of $At$ are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=-2t,\,{\lambda }_{2}=t,
$$

both of multiplicity one. Thus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}r(-2t)={e}^{-2t} \\ r(t)={e}^{t}\end{aligned}\,⇒\,{\begin{aligned}-2t{\alpha }_{1}+{\alpha }_{0}={e}^{-2t} \\ t{\alpha }_{1}+{\alpha }_{0}={e}^{t}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system for ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}:$

- Subtracting the second equation from the first one, we get

$$
-3t{\alpha }_{1}={e}^{-2t}-{e}^{t}\,⇒\,{\alpha }_{1}=-\frac{1}{3t}({e}^{-2t}-{e}^{t}).
$$

- Multiplying the second equation by $2$ and adding to the first one, we get

$$
3{\alpha }_{0}={e}^{-2t}+2{e}^{t}\,⇒\,{\alpha }_{0}=\frac{1}{3}({e}^{-2t}+2{e}^{t}).
$$

Substituting ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ into the expressions for the required entries of ${e}^{At},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{\alpha }_{1}t & =3(-\frac{1}{3t}({e}^{-2t}-{e}^{t}))t \\  & =-({e}^{-2t}-{e}^{t}) \\  & ={e}^{t}-{e}^{-2t} \\ 4{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & =4(-\frac{1}{3t}({e}^{-2t}-{e}^{t}))t+\frac{1}{3}({e}^{-2t}+2{e}^{t}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}((-4{e}^{-2t}+4{e}^{t})+({e}^{-2t}+2{e}^{t})) \\  & =2{e}^{t}-{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{t}+2{e}^{-2t} & -2{e}^{t}+2{e}^{-2t} \\ {e}^{t}-{e}^{-2t} & 2{e}^{t}-{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}].
$$
